mental_model: It flattens multi-dimensional elementwise computation into one-dimensional form: the compute stays elementwise but runs over a single flat iteration domain, with collapse operations in front of it and expansion back at the result boundaries. The pass has two engines — a greedy mode that collapses every eligible elementwise op locally, and a tidy mode that first analyzes the whole function to decide which dimensions may merge, which must stay separate, and which shapes should not be flattened at all. Downstream vectorization wants flat element streams, so this reshaping runs immediately before vector-function formation.
need: Frontend IR (linalg/HFusion) describes computation in natural multi-dimensional shapes, but the vector pipeline's fusion, masking, and register-oriented lowering all work best on uniform flat element streams. Without a dedicated shape-normalization step, every later pass would have to handle arbitrary dimensionality itself, and vector-function bodies would stay irregular.
responsibility: For one function: decide whether it should be flattened at all (core-type and guard checks), then either greedily collapse every elementwise op with more than one loop dimension, or hand the function to the analysis-driven Flattener, which computes collapse groups, rewrites the affected compute and indexing ops, and restores original shapes at the function's result boundary.
observable_outcome: Elementwise ops inside the function operate on 1-D types — e.g. ops over 32x7 buffers become ops over 224 elements behind collapse_shape ops, with expand_shape restoring original shapes where results escape; in tidy mode the collapse can be partial (groups like two-dims-then-one-dim), and register-based mode also rewrites memref loads/stores and arange to 1-D form. Shapes the analysis rejects (broadcast-into-reduce) stay multi-dimensional.

audience_contract.who: compiler engineers familiar with MLIR passes and the vectorization story, who have never read FlattenOps.cpp
audience_contract.assumed_knowledge: MLIR pass pipelines, linalg structured ops, tensor/memref reshape ops, what vector-function outlining is for
audience_contract.not_assumed: this pass's internals, the Flattener/DimensionAnalyzer implementation, Ascend NPU specifics

in the auto-schedule (non-Triton) path flatten runs inside flattenAndFold after FoldTensorEmpty, in Tidy mode without register-based

inputs.name: function in HFusion/linalg form
inputs.form: func::FuncOp whose body contains structured linalg/HFusion ops over tensor or memref types
inputs.description: the pass argument; host functions are in scope too unless skip-host applies; functions labeled AIC/AIV are out of scope

inputs.name: pipeline-configured options
inputs.form: FlattenOpsOptions: flatten-mode, skip-host, multi-dynamic-shape, register-based, use-preorder-walk-traversal, skip-scope (defaults greedy/false/true/false/true/true)
inputs.description: both regbase sites fix Tidy mode, register-based=true, multi-dynamic-shape=false; standalone users get greedy by default

inputs.name: core-type label (optional)
inputs.description: when present, AIC and AIV labels make the pass a no-op for that function

outputs.name: flattened function
outputs.form: same func.func with elementwise compute on collapsed 1-D types: collapse_shape in front of ops, expand_shape restoring result shapes at boundaries; tidy mode may use partial reassociation groups and rewrites indexing ops (slices, arange, memref load/store)
outputs.description: shape-preserving at the function boundary; external result types do not change

outputs.name: pass failure
outputs.form: signalPassFailure when greedy pattern application fails or Flattener.flatten fails
outputs.description: loud failure instead of silently continuing with unflattened IR

mechanism.summary: The pass is a two-engine dispatcher wrapped in eligibility gates: it first decides whether this function may be flattened at all (core-type label, host check, register-based unpropagateable-case check), then either applies a greedy elementwise-collapse pattern set over the whole function or delegates to the analysis-driven Flattener, which computes per-value collapse groups (possibly partial), rewrites compute and indexing ops to the flattened form, and expands results back at the boundary.

stages.name: Function eligibility gate
stages.what: queryFuncCoreType on the function: a labeled AIC or AIV function returns immediately (no flattening); unlabeled, MIX, and AIC_OR_AIV functions proceed. In tidy mode, additionally: host functions return when skip-host is set, and register-based mode returns when the function contains custom ops, complex control flow, or — when skip-scope is on — scope ops

stages.name: Greedy elementwise collapse
stages.what: flatten-mode=greedy: register the elementwise-collapse pattern for all linalg and HFusion structured ops plus linalg.generic, then applyPatternsGreedily over the function; each match requires more than one loop dim and an elementwise non-broadcast op, and rewrites it with the identity reassociation (all loop dims into one group); failure of the whole application signals pass failure

stages.name: Analysis-driven flattening (tidy)
stages.what: flatten-mode=tidy: build DimensionAnalyzerOptions{registerBased, usePreOrderWalkTraversal} and run Flattener(funcOp, options).flatten(multiDynamicShape); the engine inherits DimensionAnalyzer, keeps per-run bookkeeping (collapse sets, value replacement, delete marks, a worklist), can break collapse boundaries for sub-byte i1 values and dynamic shapes, adjusts a wide per-op surface (slices/arange/gather/scf/load/store/broadcast/reduce...), collapses block arguments, and expands tail/return values back

stages.name: Failure handling
stages.what: both engines fail loudly: failed applyPatternsGreedily and failed Flattener.flatten each call signalPassFailure

control_flow: pipeline builders add the pass at fixed points (enableFlatten-gated); runOnOperation is the sole entry
runOnOperation: core-type gate → mode dispatch (flatten-mode) → greedy engine OR tidy guards + Flattener
inside greedy mode the pattern rewriter drives individual op rewrites to fixpoint; inside tidy mode the Flattener drives its own walk and worklist
the pass never re-runs itself: each placement site adds it once per function nest
data_flow: IR in: N-D elementwise compute plus reshape/indexing ops

shape facts: the greedy pattern derives reassociation from the op's own loop count; the Flattener derives collapse groups from whole-function dimension analysis (dimension connectivity can be 'broken' by sub-byte i1 values or dynamic shapes)
IR out: collapsed 1-D compute with collapse_shape/expand_shape pairs; indexing ops' offsets/sizes/strides recomputed; original shapes restored at function-result boundaries
no values leave the function: the pass adds no results, sets no attributes, and creates no side artifacts

The tensor-form sibling case shows the boundary restore: collapse → compute on <224xf32> → tensor.expand_shape back to 32x7 before return (EV-013)

decisions.question: Which engine flattens this function?
decisions.condition: the flatten-mode option: greedy (default) or tidy
outcomes: greedy → registered pattern set + applyPatternsGreedily over the function
tidy → guard checks, then Flattener(funcOp, options).flatten(multiDynamicShape)
decisions.reason: the option is the engine selector: local per-op collapse vs whole-function analysis (option text: tidy 'will do an analysis on the entire function')

decisions.question: Should this function be flattened at all?
decisions.condition: core-type label (AIC/AIV), host-ness vs skip-host, and — in register-based tidy mode — custom ops / complex control flow / scope ops (skip-scope)
outcomes: labeled AIC or AIV → skip the whole function silently
host function with skip-host → skip (tidy mode)
register-based tidy with custom ops, complex control flow, or scope ops (when skip-scope) → skip
otherwise → proceed to the selected engine
decisions.reason: flattening rewrites indexing everywhere in a function, so functions that are already specialized or that contain constructs the flattener cannot propagate through are excluded up front

decisions.question: May this specific op collapse (greedy)?
decisions.condition: getNumLoops() > 1, isElementwise(op), and the op is not linalg::BroadcastOp
outcomes: all three hold → collapse with identity reassociation over all loop dims
already 1-D (≤1 loop) → pattern failure, no rewrite
non-elementwise or broadcast → match failure 'only elementwise flattening is supported'
decisions.reason: greedy mode deliberately has no cross-op view: a cheap local predicate decides, and an in-code TODO says the isElementwise predicate itself is due for refinement

decisions.question: How far do dimensions collapse (tidy)?
decisions.condition: whole-function dimension analysis in the Flattener (collapse-group connectivity, dynamic shapes via multi-dynamic-shape, sub-byte i1 innermost dims not multiple of 8)
outcomes: flattening would harm the computation → decline entirely (broadcast-into-reduce stays 2-D)
decisions.reason: tidy trades the greedy mode's locality for a function-wide view, so it can stop at partial groups or reject shapes that greedy would flatten

strategies.name: Greedy engine — local per-op collapse
strategies.trigger: flatten-mode=greedy (the Passes.td default; the standalone fixture uses it)
strategies.mechanism: pattern set over all linalg/HFusion structured ops + linalg.generic, applied greedily; identity reassociation over all loop dims; elementwise-only, broadcast excluded
strategies.cost: no cross-op reasoning: it may flatten shapes the tidy analysis would decline, and its isElementwise predicate is flagged for refinement in-code

strategies.name: Tidy engine — whole-function analysis
strategies.trigger: flatten-mode=tidy; the mode fixed by all three pipeline sites
strategies.mechanism: guards (host, unpropagateable case) then the DimensionAnalyzer-derived Flattener: collapse groups possibly partial, wide per-op adjustment surface, register-based mode for RegBase targets
strategies.cost: heavier analysis and a much larger engine surface; its decline conditions are only partially evidenced here (engine internals unread)

dimensions.selector: flatten-mode=greedy (default) | flatten-mode=tidy (fixed by all pipeline sites)
dimensions.scope: one op at a time, to fixpoint | one function at a time via DimensionAnalyzer-derived collapse groups
dimensions.reassociation: always full (all loop dims in one group) | can be partial ([[0,1],[2]]) or declined entirely
dimensions.op surface: registered structured elementwise ops only | also slices/arange/gather/scf bodies/memref load/store/indexing recomputation
dimensions.broadcast: excluded by the pattern | adjusted (and broadcast-into-reduce shapes declined)
dimensions.observed_output: 32x7 → 224 full collapse everywhere (fixture) | 1048576 full collapse, 1048576x1024 partial, broadcast+reduce untouched (fixture)

contracts.element: elementwise structured ops whose reshape noise is already folded — the fixed predecessor order at both regbase sites

contracts.consumer: HFusionAutoVectorizeV2Pass / OutlineVectorFunctionPass (or the auto-schedule pipeline in the non-Triton path)
contracts.element: 1-D-formed elementwise bodies (collapse/expand bounded) in the same functions, no new attributes or results
enableFlatten (run at all), enableMultiKernel (→ skip-host), skipScope (→ skip-scope); the sites fix Tidy mode, register-based=true, multi-dynamic-shape=false

constraints.statement: greedy mode only collapses elementwise, non-broadcast structured ops with more than one loop dimension
functions labeled AIC or AIV are never flattened (silent early return)
register-based tidy refuses functions containing custom ops or complex control flow, plus scope ops when skip-scope is on (default on)
external function signature and result types are preserved: collapsed values are expanded back before returns/materialization
both engines fail the pass explicitly (signalPassFailure) if the flatten fails, rather than continuing silently

invariants.statement: the pass is shape-preserving at the function boundary: it changes how computation is indexed (1-D bodies), never the function's external types

every pipeline site that adds the pass immediately follows it with canonicalization, and the canonicalization phase markers (AfterFlattenBeforeAutoSchedule / AfterAutoSchedule) encode 'flatten already ran'

boundaries.statement: greedy full collapse of registered linalg/HFusion elementwise ops (fill, map, generic, elemwise_unary pinned by the fixture); tidy partial collapse groups; register-based tidy rewriting of memref load/store and arange to 1-D

broadcast handling differs by engine: the greedy pattern excludes broadcast ops, while the tidy Flattener adjusts broadcasts and declines broadcast-into-reduce shapes entirely — the same function can behave differently under the two modes
AIC/AIV-labeled functions, host functions (with skip-host), and — in register-based tidy — functions with custom ops, complex control flow, or scope ops (with skip-scope) never get flattened
flattening non-elementwise compute (e.g. matmul-like ops): the greedy pattern emits match failure 'only elementwise flattening is supported', and already-1-D ops are skipped (≤1 loop dim)

the isElementwise predicate is coarser than intended by the authors' own TODO ('rewrite isElementwise by judging there is at least one computational elementwise op'), so greedy eligibility may misclassify ops until that refinement lands

the tidy engine's exact legality and decline rules: Flattener.cpp (272 lines) and DimensionAnalyzer were not read at HEAD; beyond the fixture-pinned outcomes, which shapes tidy accepts or rejects is not characterized here

placement.why_here: both regbase sites put the pass after the reshape-cleanup block (PropagateReshape/FoldTensorEmpty/CanonicalizeTensorReshape + canonicalization) so its analysis sees already-folded dimensions, and before vectorization consumes it — in the SIMD branch specifically between VFFusionPass and AutoVectorizeV2, so fused VF bodies are flattened just before vector functions are formed
placement.why_not_earlier: before reshape propagation and unit-dim folding the analyzer would face redundant dynamic/unit dims that could force conservative or immediately-undone collapse groups; before VF fusion there are no fused elementwise bodies to reshape
placement.why_not_later: after AutoVectorizeV2/OutlineVectorFunction the vector bodies are already formed — flattening then would mean disturbing formed vector IR (or no-ops on ≤1-loop ops), forfeiting the point of running before vectorization

key_takeaways: One pass, two engines: greedy is a local per-op collapse (elementwise-only, broadcast excluded, always full reassociation), tidy is a whole-function analysis that can produce partial collapse groups and decline shapes outright — flatten-mode selects between them.

The pass is the vector pipeline's shape normalizer: both regbase placements fix Tidy mode with register-based=true, one right after the reshape-cleanup block in buildHFusionRegBasePipeline, the other between VFFusion and AutoVectorizeV2 in the SIMD VF-fusion branch.
Its rewrites are boundary-safe: collapse_shape in front of compute, expand_shape back at results; the function's external signature never changes.

Skipping is policy, not failure: AIC/AIV-labeled functions, host functions (skip-host), and register-based-unguardable functions (custom ops, complex control flow, scopes) are left untouched without diagnostics.
The 141-line pass file is a dispatcher: the real tidy machinery lives in the Flattener/DimensionAnalyzer engine, whose internals were not read in this analysis (recorded as unknown).
design_tradeoffs: Locality vs coverage: greedy needs no cross-op analysis but both over-flattens (broadcast-adjacent shapes) and under-classifies (the in-code isElementwise TODO); tidy buys correctness of scope with a whole-function engine (EV-004, EV-014).
Loud failure: failing flatten signals pass failure instead of silently emitting unflattened IR — robustness over resilience (EV-003, EV-006).
risks: The AIC/AIV skip is a bare return: nothing distinguishes 'skipped by core-type gate' from 'nothing to do', so a pipeline change that labels functions earlier would silently disable flattening for them (EV-008).
Mode flips change outcomes: greedy excludes broadcast ops while tidy adjusts/declines them, so switching flatten-mode can flip whether a given function flattens (EV-004, EV-009, EV-014).

ir_contract.before: structured linalg/HFusion elementwise ops over multi-dimensional tensor/memref types (e.g. 32x7), plus reshape/slice/indexing ops; in tidy register-based mode also memref loads/stores and hfusion.arange on multi-dim buffers
ir_contract.after: the same elementwise compute over collapsed 1-D types (memref/tensor.collapse_shape in front; e.g. 32x7 → 224), partial reassociation groups allowed in tidy (e.g. [[0,1],[2]] → 1048576x1024), indexing ops' offsets/sizes/strides recomputed, expand_shape restoring original shapes at result boundaries; declined shapes unchanged

pass.legality: greedy per-op: >1 loop dim, isElementwise, not a broadcast op. Function-level: no AIC/AIV func_core_type label; tidy only: not (isHost && skipHost); register-based tidy only: no custom ops, no complex control flow, and no scope ops when skip-scope (hasUnpropagateableCase). Tidy collapse decisions come from the DimensionAnalyzer-derived Flattener, whose exact rules are not read here (EV-020)
pass.rewrite: greedy: collapseOpIterationDims with identity reassociation over all loop dims, replaceOp with the collapsed results. tidy: Flattener inserts collapse ops for arguments/values, runs per-op adjust* rewrites (slices/arange/gather/scf/load/store/broadcast/reduce...), expands tail/return values back, erases marked ops; failures signal pass failure

attributes.creator: none — the pass creates no attributes, named ops, or results; it is purely shape/index rewriting
attributes.consumer: not applicable on the attribute axis; downstream consumers (vectorization) read the reshaped op forms, not new metadata
